title: HR Administrator
description:
People & Operations Assistant

Caversham, Reading
£28,000 - £32,000 per annum
Full-time Office-based (5 days per week)

Reed HR are delighted to be partnering with a growing and people-focused organisation in Caversham to recruit a People & Operations Assistant.

This is an excellent opportunity for an organised and proactive HR professional looking to develop their career within a busy and supportive People team. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the employee lifecycle, ensuring HR administration is delivered accurately, efficiently and confidentially.

The Role

Reporting to the People & Operations Manager, you will provide comprehensive administrative support across all areas of HR and People Operations. This varied position offers exposure to recruitment, onboarding, employee relations, payroll administration, training coordination and HR projects.

Key responsibilities include:
- Maintaining employee records and HR systems, ensuring data accuracy and confidentiality.
- Supporting recruitment activities, onboarding and offboarding processes.
- Preparing HR documentation including contracts, letters and employee correspondence.
- Assisting with payroll administration and monthly payroll inputs.
- Monitoring and maintaining holiday and sickness absence records.
- Coordinating training activities and compliance requirements.
- Responding to employee and manager queries in a professional and timely manner.
- Supporting the review and maintenance of company policies and procedures.
- Assisting with employee relations processes and case administration.
- Producing HR reports and management information as required.
- Supporting wider People projects and initiatives across the business.

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous experience within an HR Administration, HR Assistant or People Coordinator role.
- Good knowledge of HR practices and employment legislation.
- Strong administrative and organisational skills with excellent attention to detail.
- A professional and confidential approach to handling sensitive information.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
- Strong IT skills including Microsoft Office applications.
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- A proactive approach with strong problem-solving skills.
- Payroll administration experience would be advantageous.
- CIPD Level 3 qualification or working towards this would be desirable but is not essential.

If you're an enthusiastic HR professional looking for your next challenge and keen to build your experience across the full employee lifecycle, we'd love to hear from you.

title: AAT Assistant Accountant
description:
An opportunity has arisen for an AAT Assistant Accountant with a successful accountancy practice, that is seeking to build its team. The ideal candidate will AAT qualified with at least two years' accounts experience gained within a UK accountancy firm.

As AAT Assistant Accountant, your will a part of the Corporate Team that provides high-quality services to clients and your contribution will be a valuable part of the continuing development of the practice.

The firm offers a good benefits package to include pension, healthcare, medical cash plan, death in service cover, enhanced maternity and a range of voluntary benefits. This supportive firm has flexible, hybrid working policy.

As AAT Assistant Accountant your responsibilities will include:
- Prepare statutory and unincorporated accounts for clients and complete corporation tax and partnership business tax returns and computations to deadlines
- Assist the Department Managers as required
- Identify points for manager or partner to raise with clients and to raise potential for additional services
- Finalise paperwork for dispatch to client or HMRC
- Liaise proactively with client to obtain relevant information for their accounts, ensuring attention to detail
- Monitor own job quality and quantity in line with agreed budgets and record own chargeable time and ensure maximum recovery
- Assist clients with ad hoc bookkeeping queries and other business-related matters as required

We welcome applications from those with the following, skills, experience and attributes:
- AAT level 4 qualified
- At least two years' accounts experience gained within a UK accountancy firm
- Good general IT skills and experience with using cloud accounting software such as Xero
- UK tax experience and knowledge
- Excellent communication skills
- Acute attention to detail
- Be positive, organised and analytical
- Live within an easy commute of Banbury

Submit your CV for this AAT Assistant Accountant role

Unfortunately, we cannot accept applications for this role from candidates that do not have the right to work in the UK, or require visa sponsorship, either currently or in the future. This includes those currently on a student or graduate visa.

Additionally, candidates must have experience gained within UK accountancy practice. We stipulate these criteria due to the high volume of applications from outside of the UK.

Due to the high volume of applications we receive it is not always possible to respond to unsuccessful applicants. Therefore, if we have not responded to your application within five days please assume that on this occasion your application has not been successful.

title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Management Accountant/Bookkeeper
description:

description: This is a 12-month fixed-term Band 3 Administrative Assistant post providing maternity leave cover within the Psychological Medicine Service. The role is responsible for delivering a comprehensive, professional and efficient administrative service that supports clinicians and the wider multidisciplinary team in providing high-quality patient care. The post holder will manage patient administration throughout the patient pathway, including appointment booking, referral processing, reception duties, Electronic Patient Record (EPR) management, production of clinical correspondence, maintenance of accurate patient records, and supporting compliance with Trust and national performance standards. The role is fundamental to ensuring the smooth day-to-day operation of the service and maintaining a positive patient experience. Provide a comprehensive administrative service to support the Psychological Medicine Service and multidisciplinary team. Manage patient pathways by processing referrals, booking appointments and maintaining accurate patient records using the Trust's Electronic Patient Record (EPR) systems. Monitor and manage shared email inboxes, process incoming correspondence and respond to patient, referrer and stakeholder enquiries promptly and appropriately. Support Referral to Treatment (RTT) pathways by ensuring accurate data entry, clinic preparation, patient check-in/check-out and clinic cash-up processes. Maintain high standards of data quality, confidentiality and customer service while supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the department. Work collaboratively with clinical and administrative colleagues, contributing to service improvement initiatives and providing flexible administrative support to ensure continuity of patient care MAIN PURPOSE OF POST: Patient administration underpins the patient journey and supports the clinical teams in delivering high quality patient care and can make a real difference to the patient experience. Administration: To provide primary administrative support to the clinical staff and all patients under their care of The Psychological Medicine Service, including using EPR applications, such as Appointment Book, HIM Tracking, HIM Chart Coding, Powerchart and PM Office, to manage patient pathways. To provide reception cover and act as the first point of contact for patients attending face to face appointments and meeting and greeting patient Ensuring the waiting room area is kept clean and tidy. 4. title: Administrator
description: The Key Medical Practice sits at the heart of its community in Kidlington, providing accessible, high-quality primary care to the patients and families who depend on it. As part of PML's portfolio of practices, it benefits from the resources and governance of a wider federation while retaining the personal, continuity-focused care that defines good general practice. The team delivers the full breadth of primary care services, from routine appointments and chronic disease management to urgent care and preventative health, ensuring every patient receives safe, effective, and compassionate support. Working closely with operational managers and senior leadership, the team oversees patient care delivery, appointment coordination, clinical record management, and service performance monitoring. The practice ensures that all services remain aligned with NHS standards and regulatory requirements, while upholding a commitment to delivering accessible, patient-centred care to the Kidlington community. The post-holder provides reliable and routine administrative support to ensure the smooth daily operation of the service. This role is designed for individuals with little or no prior administrative experience but who demonstrate motivation to learn, develop and contribute to team efficiency. The role supports effective communication, accurate record-keeping, and the delivery of high-quality patient and service user care in line with organisational and NHS standards. Role Accountabilities Administrative & Operational Support Provide routine clerical and administrative support to ensure the effective running of the service. Accurately complete basic administrative tasks such as filing, photocopying, scanning, and data entry. Assist with the preparation of documents, medical reports, spreadsheets, and presentations underguidance from senior staff. Information Management Maintain accurate and well-organised records, documents, and filing systems. Ensure information is updated promptly and stored in accordance with organisational and NHS policies. Handle all data responsibly, ensuring confidentiality, accuracy, and compliance with data protection and governance standards. Communication and Coordination Provide courteous, professional, and timely responses to internal and external enquiries,including patients, callers, and colleagues. Support clear communication within the team by relaying messages, sharing information appropriately, and maintaining effective channels of contact.
